claim: Confidence calibration uses Bayesian updates informed by quality signals.
Calibration dashboards track overconfidence and underconfidence gaps.
AIM-OS distinguishes four confidence types: Direction, Execution, Autonomous, and Collaborative to prevent inflation.
Calibration model tracks bias per task category (documentation, code, organizational) to adjust raw confidence.
Expected Calibration Error (ECE) measures how well-calibrated probabilistic predictions are.
Brier score decomposes into Calibration, Resolution, and Uncertainty components.
VIF uses calibrated confidence to gate work and stores updates per chapter/system.
Calibration tracking system records predicted confidence, actual outcome, and calculates error for learning.
Beta-Binomial conjugacy enables efficient confidence updates: α_new = α_old + successes, β_new = β_old + failures.
Perfect calibration requires P(success | predicted_confidence = c) = c for all confidence levels c.
Calibration algorithms include Beta-Binomial, Platt Scaling, Isotonic Regression, and Temperature Scaling.
Calibration system architecture includes Calibration Tracker, Bias Calculator, Calibration Model, ECE Calculator, and Dashboard Generator.
Calibration thresholds: ECE < 0.05 well calibrated, ECE 0.05-0.10 acceptable, ECE > 0.10 poor calibration.
Task category clustering groups similar tasks for bias estimation using features: task type, complexity, domain, tools used.
Calibration best practices include regular updates (every 20-50 outcomes), clear task categories (minimum 10 samples), and appropriate confidence type selection.
